messages:
Alex: Heads-up — customer reported they rotated their KMS key but our customer-facing audit event doesn't show the key_version. upstream KMS log has it, but the event we surface is missing it. Can we confirm coverage?
Priya: Do you have a sample event? we might be obfuscating key_id for hosted tenants. :thinking_face:
Alex: paste below (redacted):
```json
{
  "event_type": "kms.rotate",
  "user": "svc-rotator",
  "resource": "cust-789",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-12T22:14:03Z",
  "meta": { "location": "us-west-2" }
}
```
Alex: notice no key_version / key_id top-level. downstream customer UI expects a stable key tag to show in audit exports.
Ben: quick Q — are we intentionally stripping key ids for PII/compliance? last I checked we obfuscated full key material but kept identifiers.
Priya: we obfuscate raw key material. identifiers (key_id) should be present for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we swap with stable alias. looks like the ingestion pipeline may be normalizing into meta and dropping the top-level field.
Charlie: I ran a query on audit_events: `SELECT event_time, event_type, payload->>'key_version' as kv FROM audit_events WHERE resource = "cust-789" AND event_type = "kms.rotate";` output shows kv = null for recent rotates. older events (pre-2025-09) have kv populated.
Alex: so regression in the schema mapping. We need a small contract: customer-facing events for kms.rotate must include either key_version (string) OR rotation_tag in top-level metadata. this is used by Support and by exported CSVs.
Ben: propose schema bump: add top-level field `kms_key_version` (string) — fill from payload.meta.key_version if present. Backfill plan for last 90 days. keep meta for extras. backwards-compatible.
Priya: agree in principle. also add ingestion validation so events missing both fields fail ingestion with a warning that surfaces to the pipeline dashboard.
Charlie: we can backfill by replaying S3 raw events -> kafka -> ingestion. estimate 3 hours of ops work + extra storage IO cost (~$70). can run in a canary for cust-789 first.
Ben: ok, prioritize: 1) ingestion validation test, 2) small transformer change (meta -> kms_key_version), 3) backfill job. can we get an owner for the PR and the runbook update?
Alex: I will own the PR and unit + contract tests. I'll add a schema entry to audit schema doc and open a migration PR for the ingestion transformer.
Priya: I'll update the compliance matrix and check with Legal whether aliasing rules need mention in customer-facing docs.
Charlie: I'll schedule the backfill canary during low-traffic window (Sat 02:00 UTC). will post runbook steps here.
kms-bot: Automated: rotation completed for cust-789 at 2025-10-12T22:14:03Z — ksid: redacted-XXXX — logged to s3://audit-raw/2025/10/12/1762134843.json
Ben: Please also add a contract test in the audit ingestion CI that asserts `kms_key_version` exists for `kms.rotate` events. add the test to `audit-ingest/test/contracts` and block merges if it fails.
Alex: Will do. also adding a small human-readable note for Support so they can use `auditbot query --resource cust-789 --event kms.rotate` and see key version.
Priya: one more ask — if we can't include full key_id for hosted tenants, ensure we always include a stable alias or rotation_tag so customer can correlate events to their KMS UI.
Alex: yep, plan: transformer emits `kms_key_version` and `kms_key_alias` when available. I'll attach PR link once ready.
Ben: linking runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/ir-44-kms-audit-rotation (please add postmortem notes if this becomes incident related).
Charlie: backfill canary scheduled for 2025-10-18 02:00 UTC. I'll post logs and the final diff of rows updated.
Alex: thanks all — assigning follow-ups: Alex (PR + tests), Charlie (backfill canary + ops), Priya (compliance doc), Ben (CI contract test). tagging auditbot to capture thread for investigation evidence. :white_check_mark:
auditbot: Note captured — thread saved to incident evidence bundle id=ir-44-evidence-20251012
Alex: closing loop here once PR lands and canary passes. will ping channel.
